lines: Digital oscillator carrying 47 synthesis models, from analogue waveforms and wavetables to physical models, speech and drum circuits, each shaped by two parameters
Steps through the 47 models; the four-letter code of the one in use shows on the display
Detunes by up to a semitone either way
Sets the pitch in octaves, from five octaves below the middle C of the oscillator to three above it
Attenuverts the FM input, which shifts the pitch by one octave per volt at full clockwise; with META switched on it scales that input's control of the model instead
Sets the first shaping parameter of the model in use, which is the waveform sweep, the wavefolder amount, the sync interval or the filter cutoff depending on which model that is
Attenuverts the TIMBRE input, which adds to the TIMBRE knob
Sets the second shaping parameter of the model in use, which is the detuning, the feedback amount, the formant shift or the brightness depending on which model that is
A rising edge past 1V strikes the physical models and resets the phase of the other models
Sets the pitch, one volt per octave, added to the two frequency knobs
Shifts the pitch, scaled and inverted by the FM knob, one octave per volt at full clockwise
Adds to the TIMBRE knob through the MODULATION attenuverter, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the COLOR knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
The oscillator, peaking at 5V, though loudness differs from model to model
Note — the display shows the four-letter code of the model in use, and the Model menu lists all 47 codes with a description beside each one.
Note — the module is monophonic: on a polyphonic cable only the first channel is read, and the output carries one channel.
Menu — Model — picks the synthesis model from a list giving each one's four-letter display code and a short description of it
Menu — META: FM CV selects model — hands the FM input over to choosing the model, and pitch is then set by V/OCT and the frequency knobs alone
Menu — DRFT: Pitch drift — adds the slow random detuning of an analogue oscillator
Menu — SIGN: Waveform imperfections — mixes in a waveshaped copy of the output for a dirtier tone
Menu — Low CPU (disable resampling) — runs the oscillator at the engine sample rate instead of resampling from 96kHz, which costs less processing and adds aliasing
Braids.notes: The trigger input calls Strike() on the oscillator, which re-excites the physical and percussive models and resets the phase of the others. The hardware's internal AD envelope is not implemented here: the port zeroes the settings block and exposes only meta_modulation, vco_drift and signature, so no envelope is applied to level, timbre or colour. The model count is 47, not the 48 often quoted: the shape parameter is scaled to MACRO_OSC_SHAPE_LAST_ACCESSIBLE_FROM_META, which is index 46 of the 47-entry table in Braids.cpp. FM does two different jobs. With meta modulation off it is added to the pitch in volts; with it on, Braids.cpp:84 uses a tenth of the same voltage to scan the model list instead, so the same cable changes the sound rather than the tuning.

Tides.notes: Both gate outputs run inverted against the Mutable manual, which has HIGH TIDE going high at the end of the rise and LOW TIDE going high at the end of the fall, each staying high until the cycle restarts or the envelope is retriggered. The plugin holds each one high through its segment and drops it at the end, so the lines describe the plugin. Clock sync differs too: the manual engages the phase-locked mode by holding the range switch for a second, while the plugin locks to the CLOCK input whenever a cable is patched there. The Sheep firmware also disables clock sync: set_sync is called with the CLOCK input's connected state ANDed with the firmware being off.

lines: Two channels of filter and amplifier whose gain and brightness are driven from the EXCITE input by an envelope, a vactrol model, an envelope follower or a compressor
Sets the attack and decay character of that channel's function: the envelope times, the slowness of the vactrol, or the reaction time of the follower
Sets how far the filter opens and closes with the gain; past noon the modulation shrinks again and an offset replaces it, so the filter is shut fully counter-clockwise and open fully clockwise
Attenuates that channel's LEVEL input; with nothing patched there it works as a gain offset
Sets that channel's amplifier response, exponential at one end and linear at the other
One press shows that channel's function on the display, and each further press steps through envelope, vactrol, follower and compressor; holding the button switches to the second set of functions
One press brings the bargraph back to the display, and each further press steps the meter between excite, level, input and output
The control signal for that channel: the trigger for the envelope, the signal a vactrol or follower responds to, or the side-chain for the compressor
The audio for that channel; with nothing patched it reads a constant 5V, so the output carries the control signal itself
Drives that channel's amplifier directly through the LEVEL MOD attenuator; with nothing patched it reads 8V
That channel after the filter and amplifier
Note — the number of channels on whichever of the two audio inputs carries more sets how many voices the module runs, up to sixteen, and both outputs carry that many.
Menu — Link channels — makes the second channel follow the first channel's settings
Menu — Channel 1 mode — Envelope, Vactrol, Follower, Compressor, AR envelope, Plucked vactrol, Cutoff controller, Slow compressor, Direct VCF controller or Lorenz generator for the first channel
Menu — Channel 2 mode — Envelope, Vactrol, Follower, Compressor, AR envelope, Plucked vactrol, Cutoff controller, Slow compressor, Direct VCF controller or Lorenz generator for the second channel
Menu — Meter — picks what the bargraph shows: Excite, Level, In or Out
